subject: Novapax DPA / MSA: SCCs & transfer-addendum questions
messages:
From: Sophie Lemoine <sophie.lemoine@novapax.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco D'Angelo <marco.dangelo@novapax.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2028 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: DPA redlines + SCCs mapping (initial)

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Novapax is excited about Redwood's latency/price profile. Legal at our side has a couple of DPA asks that block commercial sign-off:

1) SCCs: they want to see an explicit delegation of controller/processor mapping (we've attached a short matrix) and confirmation that Redwood will not sub-process outside the EEA without prior notice.
2) Transfer-addendum: because of our French entities we need either SCCs executed or a transfer-impact addendum (TIA) that addresses KMS key residency and extra safeguards.
3) Evidence: procurement is asking for SOC2 + KMS architecture note; we can accept a redacted diagram.

I've attached our annotated redlines (initial_DPA_comments.pdf) — can you confirm Redwood's position on the three bullets above? We are hopeful to close this week if we can align.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Lemoine
Head of Legal Ops, Novapax

Attachments: initial_DPA_comments.pdf (PDF, 320KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lemoine <sophie.lemoine@novapax.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2028 10:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + SCCs mapping (initial)

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the matrix. Short answers up front:

- SCCs: Redwood can execute the current EU SCCs and we maintain a processor/subprocessor roster. We do request a limited carveout for ephemeral model-training buckets — I flagged that in the attached note.
- Subprocessing outside EEA: we have a notification commitment with a 30-day notice window for new subprocessors; we can add a clause to require written consent for transfers to non-EEA subprocessors for accounts with stricter residency needs.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II and a redacted KMS architecture diagram are available; I will attach redacted artifacts.

I'll loop in Ben (privacy/legal product) and Laura (commercial) to confirm any commercial tradeoffs for stronger residency commitments. Proposed timeline: internal legal/ops call today, and we aim to circulate a consolidated redline by EOD tomorrow.

Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redacted_KMS_diagram.pdf (PDF, 180KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2028 11:30:00 +0200
Subject: Internal: proposed fallback & limited-residency wording

Irene / Laura — quick internal note from privacy/product:

Summary of options we can offer without impacting runtime:
- Option A (preferred): Execute standard SCCs; add a short rider that requires 30-day notice before non-EEA subprocessor use and offers a temporary regional routing policy for account-level configuration (no contractual residency guarantee).
- Option B (escalation): For a revenue uplift / Dedicated reservation, we can commit to regional KMS key residency and enforce region-only serving for defined services. This requires ops changes and a time-box.

Suggested compromise language (to test with Novapax): bullet list in attached "proposed_fallback_clauses.docx" — includes a one-year review and an escape hatch for security incidents.

I'm OK with providing SOC2 + KMS diagram today. If Novapax insists on contractual residency for hosted, push for Dedicated (upgrade path).

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Privacy Product

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2028 12:05:00 +0200
Subject: RE: Internal: proposed fallback & limited-residency wording

Thanks Ben — quick commercial view:
- If we accept any explicit residency guarantee in the MSA/Order Form, it should be tied to a pricing premium or a Dedicated commitment. Otherwise we set an expectation we can't meet for hosted customers.
- Procurement will ask for acceptance criteria; we should mark any clause that materially changes SLOs or adds run-costs.

Neha — can you review the SCC delegation language and confirm if the draft rider would meet EU regulators' expectations for a customer with a French subsidiary? If not, note the blocker items.

I'll prepare a short negotiation memo for the AE to use in the call.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Operations

From: Sophie Lemoine <sophie.lemoine@novapax.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jul 2028 08:22:00 +0200
Subject: Novapax updated redlines (v3) + SCCs mapping

Team — thanks for the quick internal responses. Please find our updated redlines attached (Novapax_DPA_redlines_v3.docx) and an SCCs_mapping_20280716.xlsx that highlights delegation expectations. Key asks this round:

- Formal confirmation that Redwood will execute SCCs and keep the subprocessor roster up-to-date (explicit clause request).
- For non-EEA subprocessors: either 1) documented prior written consent per transfer-addendum OR 2) opt-in to a regional routing feature in the console plus a contractual 45-day notice.
- Request for a KMS attestation (redacted architecture is fine).

We are under a tight procurement window — if we can align before Friday EOD, legal will sign the Order Form. Happy to hop on a 30m alignment call today.

Best,
Sophie

Attachments: Novapax_DPA_redlines_v3.docx (Word, 48KB), SCCs_mapping_20280716.xlsx (Excel, 24KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lemoine <sophie.lemoine@novapax.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jul 2028 16:02:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Novapax updated redlines (v3) + SCCs mapping

Sophie — thanks and appreciate the clarity. Short decision log and next steps from Redwood:

1) SCCs & roster: Redwood will execute the EU SCCs and include an explicit subprocessor roster clause. Neha to confirm final wording but we can commit to a monthly roster update cadence and a link to the master roster.
2) Non-EEA subprocessors: we will offer the 45-day prior written notice OR the Console-based regional routing opt-in. For hosted customers the opt-in will be marketed as an operational control, not a contractual residency guarantee. For any account that requires contractual residency guarantees, we will propose Dedicated capacity (Option B) with corresponding pricing.
3) Evidence: SOC2 Type II + redacted KMS attestation will be provided via secure drive link (see related links).

Action owners and deadline:
- Neha: draft the roster + rider wording for SCCs (EOD 18 Jul).
- Ben: share proposed fallback/residency wording and the small-business pricing delta for Dedicated (EOD 18 Jul).
- Laura: update the negotiation memo and confirm whether AE should offer a 30% uplift price for Dedicated residency commitment (EOD 18 Jul).
- Irene: circulate consolidated redline and send final to Novapax for signature (target: 18 Jul close).

If any of the legal owners need leadership sign-off for exceptions (e.g., contractually binding residency for hosted), please flag escalations and cc Elena/Rishi.

Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: proposed_fallback_clauses.docx (Word, 12KB)
